description: Team Omi is building Omi AI, a climate companion helping people in Nigeria understand risks like flooding, extreme heat and heavy rainfall. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we’re using NASA Earth-system data to identify climate trends and turn them into simple, actionable insights. We’re looking for data analysts, climate scientists, AI/ML, data engineers, frontend and UI/UX developers.
summary: Omi AI is a weather and climate assistant for Nigeria that turns NASA Earth observation data into answers anyone can use. For the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, it retrieves 45 years (1981–2025) of NASA POWER (MERRA-2) temperature and rainfall records for Lagos and Edo States and tests whether they show real, statistically significant change, using the autocorrelation-corrected Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope. For example, Lagos has warmed by about 0.17 °C per decade and Edo by 0.25 °C per decade (p < 0.001), while Lagos rainfall has increased by about 75 mm per decade. At sign-up, users choose their role, and Omi explains the same data in Simple, Learn or Research mode: one clear takeaway for a farmer, charts and explanations for a student, and full statistics with CSV export for a scientist. Omi, our mascot, answers questions by text or voice. The app also offers live weather, NASA GPM IMERG rain radar, weather alerts and route weather. Local climate change is hard to see in raw data; Omi makes it visible, trustworthy and useful for everyday decisions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Omi AI helps people in Nigeria understand both today's weather and long-term climate change in their region, using NASA data.

• Climate Trend Detective: retrieves monthly NASA POWER (MERRA-2) temperature (T2M) and bias-corrected rainfall (PRECTOTCORR) for Lagos and Edo States, 1981–2025, and detects trends with the Hamed–Rao modified Mann-Kendall test (autocorrelation-corrected), Seasonal Mann-Kendall, Theil–Sen slope with 95% confidence interval, and linear regression.

• Regional comparison: Lagos (coastal) vs Edo (inland forest) side by side. Edo is warming about 1.4× faster (+0.25 vs +0.17 °C per decade, both p < 0.001). Lagos rainfall is rising (+75 mm per decade, p = 0.02); Edo shows no significant rainfall trend.

• Role-based insight modes: users choose a role at sign-up (student, researcher, educator, policy maker, farmer, everyday user). The role sets the default view (Simple, Learn or Research), which can be changed any time. Every view uses the same data and the same results; only the level of detail changes.

• Ask Omi: a text and voice assistant that runs the real analysis and explains the calculated numbers. It never invents figures.

• Live weather and safety: current conditions and hourly forecast, NASA GPM IMERG rain radar, alerts (heavy rain, thunderstorms, heat, harmattan), and weather along a route.

• Trend Detective Challenge: a learning game in which users spot real trends in NASA records.

• Data Lab: users upload their own CSV data and run the same statistical tests.

HOW IT WORKS

A Python Flask backend calls the NASA POWER API and caches responses. Analysis uses pandas, NumPy, SciPy and pymannkendall. Maps use Leaflet with NASA GIBS layers (GPM IMERG precipitation, MERRA-2 monthly fields). Live forecasts come from MET Norway, with Open-Meteo as a fallback. The responsive web app works on desktop and mobile, in light and dark mode, and is tested with 97 automated tests.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It makes local climate change visible and measurable for people who will never open a NetCDF file. It helps farmers time planting, helps city residents prepare for floods and heat, and teaches students how scientists tell a real trend from random variation. It supports SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities), SDG 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger).

CREATIVITY

Instead of a single dashboard, Omi adapts the explanation to the person reading it. Omi, our mascot, changes with the weather (sunny, cloudy, rainy, stormy, harmattan), which makes climate data friendly.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty: autocorrelation correction, confidence intervals, and clear limitations (one grid cell per state; reanalysis, not station data). Data provenance on every chart. Accessibility. Mobile-first use in Nigeria. Free data sources that need no API key.

Live app: https://omi-ai-production.up.railway.app
